chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Lester Young and his father
summary: Cootie does not think Lester's father was hard; Lester had offers from white bands but his father would not let him go.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, I'll be darned. Well, Cootie, go back to him. There's a couple of things I wanted to ask you about it. You know, Lester said, you know, that he was frightened of his father, that his father was rough on them, was hard on them, and that, in fact -- I don't know -- I saw where Lester said one time that he'd blown, and his father didn't like what he blew, and he bawled him out. And I think he bawled him out in front of people. Made him feel very bad, and said he never -- he was against his father from then on. Well, did you -- of course you were pretty young, but was he a hard man? Mr. Young?
Well, I don't think so. I don't think so, in a way of speaking. Lester wanted to leave. He had plenty of offers during the period of time I was there, to go with white bands.
And his father wouldn't let him go.
He wasn't going to pass, was he?
